title: Efficiency: clear LS20 to 40% RHAE over 3 won levels
goal: Win at least 3 levels of ls20 (the gate; short of it scores 0 regardless of efficiency) and do it with a per-level Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE) that the server's own scorecard reports as ls20's `score` field of at least 0.40 -- see https://docs.arcprize.org/methodology for the exact formula ((human_baseline_actions / ai_actions)^2, capped at 1.15x per level). Brute-force action spam that eventually wins levels is not enough: it clears the level count but not the efficiency bar, because RHAE is normalized against a human action baseline the server computes, not against anything this card guesses at.
resources: ARC-AGI-3 REST API, base https://three.arcprize.org (OpenAPI spec: https://docs.arcprize.org/arc3v1.yaml); every call needs header X-API-Key: $ARC_API_KEY (register a key at https://arcprize.org/platform -> profile -> API Keys). Confirmed public games as of this investigation (2026-08-22): ls20 ("LS20", agent reasoning), ft09 ("FT09", elementary logic), vc33 ("VC33", orchestration) (https://docs.arcprize.org/available-games). The official benchmarking harness reports ~25 public games total, but only these three have an investigation-confirmed id -- see examples/frontier_arc3/README.md for the full provenance note; this card's sealed game_ids.txt draws only from the confirmed three, never from the unverified longer list.

assets/gc-471/game_ids.txt (sealed allowlist for this card: ls20, one code per line; grade.py fails the whole scorecard closed if any environment in it carries a game id whose code is not on this list).

assets/gc-471/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: reads runs/gc-471/scorecard_id.txt for the scorecard id this attempt produced, does a live GET https://three.arcprize.org/api/scorecard/<that id> with X-API-Key, and prints the metric as its last JSON line -- the verdict is the server's own record, never a local file the agent wrote).

run protocol: POST /api/scorecard/open once per attempt, drive the sealed game(s) with POST /api/cmd/RESET then ACTION1..ACTION7 per the OpenAPI spec, POST /api/scorecard/close when done, then write the returned card_id -- and nothing else -- as the first line of runs/gc-471/scorecard_id.txt before running the grader. Opening a second scorecard and grading whichever one scored higher is exactly what the sealed-allowlist check and the process expectations below are for.

python package arc-agi==0.9.9 pinned (https://pypi.org/project/arc-agi/0.9.9/) -- optional convenience toolkit (arc_agi.Arcade / EnvironmentWrapper) for driving RESET/ACTION calls; the grader itself is pure stdlib + REST and does not import it.

network: https://three.arcprize.org must be reachable at grade time; rate limit 600 req/min, HTTP 429 on excess (https://docs.arcprize.org/rate_limits). Interactive step cost is real here, unlike the static ARC-AGI-2 grid cards in frontier_arc: every RESET and ACTION call is a real turn against a live session, so budget your ACTION count and wall time, not just LLM tokens -- this is the 'interactive step cost' the horizon/budget tiers below are asked to reflect.
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-471/plan.md before the first RESET, naming per-game priorities and the exact verification command.
A written strategy log per game: what the first few frames showed, the rule/plan derived from them, and -- for every hypothesis an ACTION result falsified -- the id of the revision that replaced it.

The grader was actually executed at least twice against the closed scorecard in runs/gc-471/scorecard_id.txt -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.

runs/gc-471/scorecard_id.txt names exactly one scorecard for this card's attempt; the run log shows only that one was ever opened and graded -- opening several and keeping the best is not a legitimate use of the sealed-allowlist check.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-471/ledger.json records every RESET, per-level action counts, and outcome (WIN/GAME_OVER/timeout), including abandoned attempts and failed grader runs.

The strategy log states, for the levels that count toward the gate, what actions were skipped or shortened relative to a naive/brute-force approach -- efficiency has to be a deliberate choice the log shows, not an accident of RHAE reporting.
